chapter: Russell and Armstrong years, Goodman and the road
title: How Goodman became big; whites uptown
summary: He says there was little white jazz downtown, so whites came uptown.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: How did he get his start? What made him such a big person then?
He just kept on trying until he got where he was. That's the only way you can do.
Oh you mean how did he get his start? That I don't know.
No, I just wondered. I'm talking about, why is it at that particular time that Benny Goodman was such a big deal. You know, people must have thought that he was a great clarinet player.
Maybe they did. 'Cause they didn't have no real jazz white musician downtown then. They didn't have them.
What kind of music were they playing? You said Beer Barrel Polka and all that kind of stuff. But there wasn't no
Very little. You find jazz - that's why they came uptown. There was as many white people up here as there were Negros then. The Negros put them out.
